sections.text: In front of Bhishma and Drona, and all the rulers of the earth, said: O Arjuna (son of Pritha), behold these Kurus gathered together.
Then, Arjuna (son of Pritha) saw there (in the armies) stationed, fathers and grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons and friends too.
(He saw) fathers-in-law and friends also in both the armies. The son of Kunti, Arjuna, seeing all those kinsmen thus standing arrayed, spoke this, sorrowfully filled with deep pity.

We had been discussing Chapter 1, Arjuna Vishada Yoga, the Yoga of Arjunas Grief. So far, we have seen that Sanjaya has given us the narration of whats happening, whats happening in the palace, and whats happening at Kurukshetra on the battlefield. Hes basically giving us the mental status of each main character in this conflict.
Weve seen Dhritarashtra first, then Duryodhana, then Arjuna. We have also seen that Arjuna told Krishna to take his chariot and place it in the middle of the two armies. What we have seen so far is that both Arjuna and Duryodhana have strong egos.
One had negative qualities associated with the ego, the other positive qualities. Thats the only difference. Therefore we see Arjuna commanding or giving an order to Krishna: Place my chariot in the middle of the two armies. How do you know that Arjuna had a big ego? We also see in Mahabharata that Arjuna was the one who objected to competing with Karna.
He said, Sutaputra, I will not compete with him. When they had this competition, thats what Duryodhan gave Karna kingdom of Angadish. So he became Angaraj Because Duryodhan see an opportunity having someone equivalent to Karna Arjuna in his own side. Thats how Arkarna became Duryodhanas best friend.
Yotsamana avekhse aham. I want to see ya eta itra sama Gataha the people who are gathered here. Dhartra rashtra syedurbuddehe yudde priyachi kir savah.
Those who are gathered here just to please this evil minded Duryodhana. The very words shows his anger, hatred and his own ego. At this point he sees the army on the other side is one homogeneous mass of evil.
Because their leader is evil, Duryodhana is evil and all who are gathered on that side are just there to please Duryodhana there is no other motive. Arjuna can see this is the entire army. On the other side is nothing but people with evil intentions.
They are either themselves an evil or theyre just supporting evil for whatever the personal gain or whatever the personal opinion. And now we hear from Sanjay. He gives a very unbiased commentary.
He is a commentator just like our news. People claim that all always give is the news. We are not news ourselves.
We are not putting our coloring. Sanjaya, Vaacha, Evam, Uktva, Hrushikeshah, Guda, Keshena. This is what told by Arjuna to Hrishikesha.
Hrishikesha is the one who has the control of the senses. Thats one interpretation. Other is the one who has the short hair Gudakesha, one who has the control over sleep on his conquered sleep.
There is no real proof in Mahabharata in Arjunas biography that he has conquered sleep. The Western scholars said they won with the hair in bundles. Hair in style bundles.
Obviously in India we have not seen that hairstyle. But here we can see the African Americans have hair in bundles. So its possible that Vedvyas Bhagavan is just saying what they look like and not have this deeper meaning.
We have a tendency to find deeper meaning in everything we see in our scriptures. In my first year of architecture there were simple tasks like design a handle for a window or a doorknob. And then we obviously made very complicated designs because otherwise how are you going to impress your teacher? So we have a tendency to complicate things and see deeper meaning than what is actually there.
It is possible that Bhagavan Vedavyasa simply described how these two people looked. So, having been thus addressed by Arjuna, Krishna responded. Oh, Bharata Bharada here is addressed to Dhritarashtra because he was the king of Bharatkand.
It has been said that Kuru dynasty was the first to organize the society in a statewide society. So Bharata, you are the king of this Bharat Khan Senayoho Ubhayoho Madhya Sapayitva Rathautamam. So we have the confirmation from Sanjay that Krishna followed the order thus ordered by Arjuna.
Krishna placed the chariot in the middle of the two armies. Bisma Drona, Pramukhataha, Sarve Samcha, Mahikshitam, Vacha Partha Pasheta, Samavetaan, Kurunithi. He put it right in front of Bhishma and Drona.
He could have put it right in front of Duryodhana instead. And then Krishna spoke the first words uttered by him in Bhagavad Gita. This is the only time we hear Krishnas words indirectly through Sanjaya; otherwise we hear his direct words as Sri Bhagavan Uvacha. But here Sanjaya reports what Krishna said to Arjuna: Pashyaitan, make sure you see all the Kurus who are gathered here. Look at Vishwa and Drona and other kings, but also see all the gurus gathered here.
Because what was Arjunas intention? He just wanted to see who are against him. He wanted to see who are gathered here to please this evil Duryodhana. He very clearly said, thats all I want to see.
I want to make sure that I understand who Im fighting with. Therefore Krishna put him right in front of the Bhishma Dranada. Its not the homogeneous mass of evil that youre facing that once you wipe out that evil, things will be just well and good.
There wont be any problems, no side effects. Everything will be just good. So this is how we also save the world.
We think that if we eradicate the evil from this world, well, we have learnt in last few years, eradicating anything doesnt solve anything unless the cause for the evil is eradicated. Just eradicating the other side completely will not solve the problem. It may create more problems, but you have to be prepared for that.
You should know what you are dealing with. Therefore he put Arjunas cherry right in the Bhishma and Drona because they are clearly not part of evil. But the more important he said, see all the Kurus who are gathered here.
Arjuna himself was a Kuru. He was the descendant of the Kuru dynasty. Both Gauravas and Pandavas are descendants of Kurt dynasty.
Up till now we have heard Arjuna referring to Kaurava as Dhartrastranam, Dhritarashtras sons. His animosity was against Dhritarashtras son, not against Kuru. Therefore, in the previous time when Arjuna has fought with even Bhishma, there was not really big problem.
Basically protecting Virats kingdom and he fought with Bheeshma. He didnt have any problem fighting with Bheeshma before. Obviously he didnt try to kill him, but we couldnt kill him anyway.
But this time Krishna says, look at all the Kurus. Dont only look at Dhrutrastras putra. He gives him instruction indirectly.
Make sure that you are aware that all your family members are involved on both sides in the next two verses. Tatra apasyat, sthitan, parthah, pitru, Nathaha, pita, Mahan, acharya, matulan, bhrartran, putran, patran, sakimsthata. So now he is obviously observing on both sides that he doesnt see just the evil and good divided by the line.
This is what we do in our life. We divide this world of liking and disliking with an imaginary line in my mind that if I can avoid this which I dont like, the world will be nothing. My life will be nothing but pure happiness.
Well, we tend to forget that those are intertwined with each other. The world which I like and world which I dont like, they intertwined with each other. So some of us in elections are party line voters because we clearly see that this side is a side of good, that side is side of not so good.
Its only when you find out that the world is not as clearly divided into good and evil as we like to think. In our childhood we had its very simple who are bad people, who are good people, cowboys and Indians. But world is not like that.
Krishna wants to make sure the Arjuna understands that. There is also another implication which we heard from lots of commentators that as we have seen that Arjunas words indicate he has a big ego. Big ego doesnt mean the person is necessarily bad.
Good people have big egos. Artists have big egos, architects have big egos. Its actually said in our profession, unless there are any Gita, its generally said in our profession that you cant have two architects in the same room.
Their egos are so big that no room in this world is large enough to contain two egos of the two architects at the same time. I learned hard way that when we collaborate with other firms, two architects collaborate with each other and its a lesson in humility. I was fortunate enough to get this lesson very early on in my career when I came here.
So when I was in Dallas, when I first came and working with a very large firm, WZMH somewhat specialized in high rise. And we were collaborating IM Pei, an international architect and he was a design architect. WZMH was just basically an architect of record.
So I asked my boss, I said Mark, we are capable to design this project and we had the relationship with the developer, why do we have to bring in Im Pei in the mix? And he said, Rajan, 100% of zero is still zero. If you want the whole enchilada, but youre not going to get it. He said you didnt get anything.
Is it better to have a portion of an enchilada to devise a situation where at least you have a portion of the pie? So by myself I wont get that project. By themselves, they wont get the project. Well, lets compromise and say look, we can share this and we have to control our ego.
If we share this, then we both get something out of it. So the people with big egos are bipolar in nature. So they go from supreme courage to complete vulnerability in one moment.
If they see the world from this side, they will be very courageous. And when they see the competition, they see their own shortcoming. They will break down very easily.
So Krishna saw that Arjuna is overconfident. He thinks hes the best archer in the world. He has fought Bismar before.
He has done all these people. There is nothing which can stop me from wiping out this sea of evil which I see in front of me. But he had to be brought to his senses and brought to humility so that he is really prepared to fight this war.
So Krishna said, now look at the Bisma, Drona, all other kings and all the crews, all the Kurus include all the people on his side as well. Now Arjuna sees all the people and individually recognize what his relationship with them. Tatra, Apasyat, Parthaha, Pitrunatha, fatherly relatives, Pita Mahan, also grandfatherly relatives, Acharyan, teachers, Mathulan, maternal relatives, Bratan, Putran, Pautran, Sakimstatha.
Both sides he says people who are like his sons and also his grandsons, friends, Tatha, Swasuran, Sruhada, Chaeeva, also in laws, the people who are close to you. Now we have confirmation then not only he looked at the Kauravas army, he also looked at Pandavas army. He saw all the people who are dear to him, close to him, related to him.
There is no indication he sees evil here. He didnt say oh, I also see Duryodhani. All he saw is the people who are related to him, were closer to him, were dear to him.
And therefore he says Krupaya Pariya Vishtaha, Visidantam Idam Abravit. He thus sorrowfully filled with deep pity said this Sanjay is actually generous in calling him as a deep pity he may be broken down by his own insecurities. Now he realized that the world is not divided into evil and good, but a mixture of both on all sides.
Things which we consider evil and lots of good in it and things we consider good has some evil in it.

These verses describe Arjunas expanded vision. He now sees pitrin (fathers), pitamahan (grandfathers), acharyan (teachers), matulan (maternal uncles), bhratrin (brothers), putran (sons), pautran (grandsons), sakhin (friends), shvasuran (fathers-in-law), and suhridah (well-wishers), on BOTH armies. The clear line between us and them dissolves. What seemed like a righteous battle against evil Duryodhana now reveals itself as a civil war within one family. Offers a deeper insight here: people with big egos are bipolar in nature, they swing from supreme confidence to complete vulnerability in one moment. Arjuna, the greatest archer in the world who just commanded Krishna confidently, now sees reality differently and begins to crumble. His previous confidence wasnt based on comprehensive understanding but on a simplified view of the situation. Reflect on moments when your certainty suddenly collapsed upon seeing a situation more completely. Perhaps you were confident about a decision until you truly considered its impact on everyone involved. Perhaps you were sure about a course of action until you recognized the faces on the other side. This isnt weakness, its the beginning of wisdom. But the Gita will show that we cant stop here, paralyzed between action and inaction. The question becomes: how do we act with full awareness of complexity, without being paralyzed by it? Thats the teaching that will unfold. For now, sit with the discomfort of seeing your own battlefield more completely. What relationships, what costs, what complications have you been choosing not to see?
